title: Normalized inverse-image and coefficient transport for internal normed modules
statement:
Work in compatible small-site and coefficient universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $F$ be a normed field with totally disconnected metric topology, let $C_F(P)=C(P,F)$ on profinite sets [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and put $F_T=p_T^*C_F$ for every scheme $T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal $F_T$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], relative tensor [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor, def-sfb-modobj-symmetric-tensor], and the module inverse image $f_F^*=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_{f,F}}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(f^{-1})$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback].

Let $F\hookrightarrow F'$ be a continuous inclusion into another totally disconnected normed field. It induces ring-object maps $a_T:F_T\to F'_T$ by postcomposition on continuous functions [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]. For every scheme $T$ the functor $r_T=\operatorname{Res}_{a_T}$ [def-sfb-modobj-restriction] is exact and additive, and is the identity on underlying abelian sheaves and maps. For any scheme morphism $f:Y\to X$, the coefficient comparisons are ring-object isomorphisms and satisfy
$$\alpha_{f,F'}\circ f^{-1}a_X=a_Y\circ\alpha_{f,F}.$$

Write $E_T^F$ and $E_T^{F'}$ for the canonical equivalences to modules over the reconstructed section-ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Under these equivalences, $f_F^*$ is canonically identified with the abelian inverse image $f^{-1}$ whose $F_Y$-action is the transported action through $\alpha_{f,F}^{-1}$; likewise for $F'$. The comparison is the scalar-isomorphism identification
$$F_Y\otimes_{f^{-1}F_X}f^{-1}M\xrightarrow{\sim}f^{-1}M,\qquad b\otimes m\longmapsto\alpha_{f,F}^{-1}(b)m.$$
It respects addition, scalar multiplication and the regular-module units. The analogous internal/sectionwise identifications of coefficient restriction and scalar extension send $b'\otimes m$ to the same balanced generator for the sheaf tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

There is a natural isomorphism $f_F^*r_X\xrightarrow{\sim}r_Yf_{F'}^*$. After the displayed identifications its underlying abelian-sheaf map is the identity of $f^{-1}N$, and its $F_Y$-action is explicitly the $f^{-1}F'_X$-action precomposed with the common map
$$f^{-1}a_X\circ\alpha_{f,F}^{-1}=\alpha_{f,F'}^{-1}\circ a_Y.$$
For $x:s=\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$, $k$ algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point], constant sections therefore give
$$\Gamma(s,x_F^*r_XN)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{F'/F}\Gamma(s,x_{F'}^*N)$$
with identity underlying additive map. These comparisons apply termwise and descend to the ordinary unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. No boundedness, constructibility, completeness or flatness assumption on $F_X\to F'_X$ is imposed.

proof.text: Postcomposition by the continuous inclusion gives a morphism $a:C_F\to C_{F'}$ of commutative condensed rings. Pulling it back gives $a_T=p_T^*a$. The maps $\alpha_{f,F}$ and $\alpha_{f,F'}$ are isomorphisms of ring objects, not merely of abelian sheaves. By [def-sfb-alpha] they are components at $C_F,C_{F'}$ of one natural comparison $f^{-1}p_X^*\cong p_Y^*$. Its naturality at $a$ says precisely $\alpha_{f,F'}\, f^{-1}a_X=a_Y\alpha_{f,F}$. Composing on the left and right with the respective inverse components gives $f^{-1}a_X\,\alpha_{f,F}^{-1}=\alpha_{f,F'}^{-1}a_Y$. This uses arbitrary commutative condensed rings, so it does not require that the fields be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$.

source.place: Section 3, printed p.6, Example 3.1 and the two adjunction paragraphs; explicit ordinary-category normalization by Q35

proof.text: The equivalences $E_R$ to section-ring module sheaves leave underlying abelian sheaves and maps unchanged. Restriction along a ring-object map $a:R\to S$ replaces the action by $\gamma_N(a\otimes1)$, so on sections it is exactly restriction along the reconstructed ring-sheaf map. For extension, [def-sfb-modobj-extension] takes the coequalizer of the two $R$-action arrows on $S\otimes R\otimes M\rightrightarrows S\otimes M$. The comparison of [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison], applied to $R$-modules $S,M$, identifies the relative tensor and its local generators with the sheafified sectionwise balanced tensor. Its formula is $s\otimes m\mapsto s\otimes m$. The additional $S$-action agrees: acting by $s'$ on the first factor gives $(s's)\otimes m$ on both sides. Thus this is also an $S$-linear comparison for extension of scalars. The same tensor comparison identifies the regular module with the section ring and preserves its unitors. These are the internal/sectionwise coefficient identifications claimed in the statement; sheaf tensor sections need only be locally sums of pure tensors.

source.place: Section 3, printed p.6, Example 3.1 and the two adjunction paragraphs; explicit ordinary-category normalization by Q35

proof.text: Fix $M$ and set $P=f^{-1}M$, $A=f^{-1}F_X$, $B=F_Y$, $\alpha=\alpha_{f,F}$. The internal/sectionwise pullback comparison identifies the specified module pullback with $B\otimes_A P$. Give $P$ the transported $B$-action $b\cdot p=\alpha^{-1}(b)p$. The formula $c(b\otimes p)=\alpha^{-1}(b)p$ is balanced since $\alpha^{-1}(b\alpha(a))p=\alpha^{-1}(b)ap$, and it is $B$-linear since $c(b'b\otimes p)=\alpha^{-1}(b')c(b\otimes p)$. It extends uniquely through the sheafified tensor. The map $u(p)=1\otimes p$ is inverse: $cu(p)=p$, while $uc(b\otimes p)=1\otimes\alpha^{-1}(b)p=b\otimes p$ by balancing. These formulas commute with restrictions and module morphisms, hence give a natural isomorphism. They preserve sums and send $b\otimes1$ in the regular-module tensor to $\alpha^{-1}(b)$; composing with $\alpha$ gives the usual regular unit map $b\otimes a\mapsto b\alpha(a)$. Thus the regular-module unit normalization also agrees. Repeat with $F'$.

source.place: Section 3, printed p.6, Example 3.1 and the two adjunction paragraphs; explicit ordinary-category normalization by Q35

proof.text: Exactness can be checked on underlying abelian sheaves. Indeed [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] makes each $E_R$ exact, and the sectionwise forgetful functor is faithful and exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. It reflects isomorphisms: the inverse of an invertible underlying additive sheaf map $v$ is linear because $v(rx)=r v(x)$ implies $v^{-1}(ry)=r v^{-1}(y)$. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-jointly-reflect-short-exact], for a singleton family of these forgetful functors, says that a module short sequence is exact if and only if its underlying abelian-sheaf sequence is exact. Restriction $r_T$ preserves addition of maps and is identity on these underlying sheaves and maps by step 2, so it is additive exact. The normalized pullback of step 3 has underlying functor the exact abelian inverse image of [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-exact]; its action on sums of maps is that same inverse image. Thus $f_F^*$ and $f_{F'}^*$ are additive exact as well. None of these arguments tensors along $a_T$ to test exactness, so no flatness of $a_T$ is involved.

source.place: Section 3, printed p.6, Example 3.1 and the two adjunction paragraphs; explicit ordinary-category normalization by Q35

proof.text: For an $F'_X$-module $N$, both composites in the proposed comparison normalize to the same abelian sheaf $f^{-1}N$. On $f_F^*r_XN$ its action is the $f^{-1}F'_X$-action precomposed with $f^{-1}a_X\,\alpha_{f,F}^{-1}$: this follows by applying the formula for transport of an action in [sk-def-sfb-transport] to $\gamma_N(a_X\otimes1)$. On $r_Yf_{F'}^*N$ it is that action precomposed with $\alpha_{f,F'}^{-1}a_Y$. Step 1 equates these ring maps. The identity of $f^{-1}N$ is therefore $F_Y$-linear in both directions and natural in $N$. Conjugating it by the two contractions of step 3 gives the required natural isomorphism of the original module functors. Its underlying map after normalization is literally the identity, rather than an unspecified linear automorphism.

source.place: Section 3, printed p.6, Example 3.1 and the two adjunction paragraphs; explicit ordinary-category normalization by Q35

proof.text: Take $f=x:s\to X$. Applying sections on $s$ to the isomorphism of step 5 leaves its underlying additive map equal to the identity. The constant functions on the one-point profinite set identify $C_F(*)=F$ and $C_{F'}(*)=F'$. Their pullbacks to $s$ give the constant-section scalar maps $F\to\Gamma(s,F_s)$ and $F'\to\Gamma(s,F'_s)$; functoriality of pulled-back coefficients and postcomposition give $a_s(c_b)=c_{a(b)}$ for $b\in F$. Thus restricting the section-module actions through these constant-section maps turns the $F_s$-linear comparison into exactly $\Gamma(s,x_F^*r_XN)\cong\operatorname{Res}_{F'/F}\Gamma(s,x_{F'}^*N)$, still identity on the additive group. This argument applies in particular when $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ with $k$ algebraically closed. It uses neither an equivalence of all point sheaves with vector spaces nor exactness of global sections.

source.place: Section 3, printed p.6, Example 3.1 and the two adjunction paragraphs; explicit ordinary-category normalization by Q35

proof.text: Apply every additive functor and natural comparison above degree by degree to a cochain complex. Naturality for each differential makes each comparison a chain isomorphism, with inverse given degree by degree by the same inverse comparison. Step 4 supplies exactness for coefficient restriction and normalized inverse image; the equivalences $E_R$ are exact as well. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] their termwise functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms on all unbounded complexes and descend to the ordinary derived categories. The localization universal property in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] descends the chain comparisons and their inverses (their naturality survives inversion of quasi-isomorphisms). The formulas on localized representatives are the same formulas as before localization, in particular the identity comparison on the common underlying inverse-image complex. This proves the derived assertion without restricting degrees or imposing completeness, constructibility or flatness. For the point-section comparison, [lem-sfb-normed-point-exact-monoidal] gives exact additive sections $E_F$ and $E_{F\prime}$ on $s$ for these arbitrary normed coefficients. The same factorization theorem therefore also descends the termwise point-section comparison of step 6 to ordinary unbounded derived categories of abstract vector spaces. No assertion of exact sections on a general scheme is needed.
